title: Snow Bunny: moonlit ski game made in 24hrs for AI game jam
author: Slackluster
selftext:
# Snow Bunny: moonlit ski game made in 24hrs

Snow Bunny is a small endless downhill game I made for the AI Browser Game Jam. You play a witch's familiar, a little black bunny who's nicked her broom and rides it like a snowboard down a moonlit mountain. Carve the turns for speed, launch off crests, spin for moonlight, and reach the next checkpoint before the timer runs out.

The jam theme was Familiar, and I took it about as literally as it goes.

With a little under 24 hours left, I gave the AI a prompt and asked it to forge a design document. I started with only an idea of a bunny skiing down a mountain, like SSX but simpler. This was a fast one, but still turned out surprisingly well because I kept the scope small. ​

# One engine draws, another does everything else

This is the part worth stealing. The 3D scene is Three.js. Everything around it (input, sound, vector math, timers) is LittleJS.

The trick is letting each do only what it's good at. Three.js draws a lovely scene and ignores everything else. LittleJS covers all the stuff you'd otherwise rebuild every jam: keyboard, gamepad, and touch arrive through one input layer, and ZzFX hands you sound effects for free. AI wrote almost none of it, freeing it up to focus on the game instead of the scaffolding.

There's no art assets in the project, not one model or texture. The bunny, trees, rocks, and moonlight pickups are all spheres, cones, and boxes under a single moon light. Primitives look great when you commit to them and keep a consistent simple design.

# Built in layers, playable the whole way down

I added one thing at a time and made each feel right before stacking the next. First, just a slope and gravity: a mountain you slide down, nothing else. Once the sliding felt good on its own, on went the jump, then air spins, then the moonlight pickups and a meter to spend on a boost. Checkpoints and the timer came last, and that's the bit that turned an endless drift into something with a pulse.

Keeping it playable at every step is the secret. You always know right away whether the last change helped.

# Where the time went

Not the features but the feel. How forgiving a landing should be, how sharply you can turn at speed, and how much to smooth the camera so the bumps don't turn your stomach. None of that lands on the first try. It's just play, nudge, play again, a hundred times over. Since the jam I've mostly been tidying up the mobile and touch controls.

For the record, the art, music, and a good chunk of the store copy are AI-generated, which is the whole point of this jam. Even the cover image was generated in one shot with only a few minor tweaks.

# Go do a jam

If you've never tried one of these, the AI Browser Game Jam is a soft landing. It's deliberately low-pressure: free browser games, any AI tools you like for code, art, music, or sound, and no sponsor strings. Most jams that allow AI make you use whoever's paying for the jam. This one doesn't. It keeps growing, too: 50 people the first time, more than a hundred by the second, plus a Discord where folks trade process notes. Watch the #AIGameJam tag and jump into the next one. A weekend and a willingness to tweak something like the camera fifty times is all it takes.

Play Snow Bunny here: [https://focaccai.itch.io/snow-bunny](https://focaccai.itch.io/snow-bunny)

Find the jam here: [https://itch.io/jam/ai-game-jam-3](https://itch.io/jam/ai-game-jam-3)

replies.body: So they are a head of the curve because have you seen devs of triple A studios play their games. Blizzard use to have a series of it for D4 until they kept getting called out that the devs playing clear never even touched the game.

comments.author: Prior-Meeting1645
comments.body: Where did you get the soundtrack from?

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
i made the music with suno. i asked claude to create a few chill music prompts for my game. i just tried about 10 songs and picked the one i liked most. there is a separate track for main menu. this was the prompt for game music...

>Ambient electronic with slow 86 BPM pulse, warm analog pads, glassy mallet arpeggios, and a breathing sub-glow; verse-like sections stay nearly empty, then the arrangement gently opens with twinkling bell runs and brushed heartbeat percussion before settling back into drifting pad haze, Breathy tails, soft wind texture, close-intimate stereo bloom, seamless loopable and weightless, warm, slow, mallet, ambient, deep, emotional, low, soft, hypnotic, light, magical, electronic, faint, relaxing, gentle.

comments.author: Both_Introduction_28
comments.body: How you did you create the snowy terrain? 😎

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: the terrain uses a random noise field height map applied a grid mesh, i ended up going with equilateral triangles instead of the more common 45 degree triangles to give it a cleaner look. the code uses the same height field for physics and placing objects.

comments.author: Sebguer
comments.body: you might want to look up what this phrase means on urban dictionary hahahaha

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
i did my research. a white girl that is into black guys? basically a phrase that no one has ever heard and that doesn't even make much sense. i had to look it up again to make sure it wasn't something actually bad.

maybe you haven't named many things, but the fact is whatever you name something if you do proper research then you are bound to find some sort of conflict and you just need to decide on whether it is worth thinking of another name.

in this case i like the name well enough but feel free to suggest a better one.

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body: Snow bunny is a really well known term bro, please trust us on this people will be making fun of the title the entire time. Try looking up synonyms for Snow, and combining them with either Bunny or Rabbit. Blizzard Bunny kinda has a ring to it

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
"A Blizzard Bunny is a reference to a snow bunny but in this case she likes getting a train ran on her by a group of black men; A persons who’s interest comes from black men in large groups having sexual relations." [https://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=Blizzard+Bunny](https://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=Blizzard+Bunny)

not only that but blizzard entertainment is one of the most well known game studios.

this is why you need to just accept that whatever the term is, there will be potential conflicts and red flags. your idea is much worse.

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body: Do whatever you want then I don't care anymore, if multiple people are going to try and help you avoid people making fun of your game and that's the best response you have, then you deserve to be made fun of.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
hey, sorry i didn't take your suggestion with more thoughtful care. i was frustrated that so many people are telling me the name is bad, when i went through about 10 other names that i would rather have used but had to abandon for various reasons after i did vetting. then i was maybe happy to feel validated that your name ended up having and even more offensive urban dictionary definition. i thought it over and want to apologize, i appreciate your effort!

i will think on it and maybe come up with a better name if i decide to spend more time working on this game.

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body: No worries man, I respect you a lot for that response and I appreciate it. For what it's worth, Snow Bunny would be a good name if it weren't for having a well known double meaning. Unless you sort of leaned into the gooner demographic but this doesn't seem like the type of game or situation where you'd be comfortable doing that lmao.

comments.author: Turbulent-Stretch881
comments.body:
I think you did a fantastic job. Although a bit biased as I see a lot of my own pipeline in what you did so obviously it was fascinating to read/see.

My gripe with browser games is that code is fully exposed, right? Somehow puts a bad taste.

Is your background software dev?

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
thanks! the code is also minified and mangled so it's not of very much use to anyone. like all code it can be reverse engineered but requires some serious effort to do that. anyone with that skill would probably rather make their own game.

yes, i have an extensive career in software and have participle in over 50 game jams. so quite a bit of experience in the area of rapid game prototypes.

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body: all the objects in the game are composed of simple primitives. the bunny is a bunch of spheres, trees are a few cones stacked on top of each other. no textures!
